category: SEC Football — It Just Means More
prompt: Your wedding was scheduled the same day as the Georgia-Florida game. Explain to your fiancée why the venue has TVs now.
response:
*sits down, takes a deep breath*

Okay, babe. Before you say anything, just... hear me out.

You know how you asked why the venue coordinator emailed about "AV equipment additions"? So. Funny story.

When we picked October 26th, I genuinely did not check the schedule. I swear on my mother's life. But then Uncle Ray called, and then your DAD called—your dad, not mine!—and apparently there was some kind of... coalition forming.

Here's the thing: nobody was going to miss our wedding. But I started getting concerned that during cocktail hour, half the guest list would be huddled in the parking lot around somebody's phone, and honestly? Your cousin Derek was going to do it anyway. At least this way it's contained.

So the TVs are ONLY in the cocktail hour space. Not the ceremony. Not the reception hall. I made them put that in writing. The ceremony is sacred. When you walk down that aisle, every eye is on you, I promise. Kickoff is at 3:30, we're saying vows at 2:00—the math works.

And look, if we time the toasts right, nobody even needs to know the score until—

*pauses*

...Okay, yes, I want to know the score too. It's the Cocktail Party of the Year, honey. It's Georgia-Florida. My father took me to that game every year since I was seven. It's basically a religious observance.

But YOU are the most important thing happening that day. The game is just... ambient. Background. Like a very passionate string quartet.

Also—and I want credit for this—I turned down the venue's offer to do a "score update" during the reception. I have LIMITS.

...We're good? We're good, right?

Go Dawgs. I mean—I love you.
